papers.summary: Introduces decoupled nuclear-norm spectral weight decay. In 124M–500M LLaMA models, it reports lower effective rank and better low-rank compression at matched validation loss, alongside noisy-label accuracy gains.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses spectral regularization, training for compressibility, and memorization under label noise.

evidence.quote: Across LLaMA models with 124 124 M to 500 500 M parameters, spectral weight decay improves low-rank compression and inference speed over standard weight decay at matched validation loss.
At 60 % 60\% label noise, mean clean-test accuracy gains over matched ℓ 2 \ell_{2} regularization reach 17.78 17.78 points on MNIST and 4.59 4.59 points on four BERT-base tasks.

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: Learns compression subspaces end-to-end while freezing pretrained weights. At 70% linear-layer compression, the authors report better Llama-2-7B perplexity and zero-shot accuracy than their strongest baseline.
papers.relevance: A direct comparison point for low-rank weight compression and quality-preserving factorization, though not a pretraining method.

evidence.quote: All projectors are optimized jointly against a global objective—the KL divergence to the dense model’s output distribution or the model’s original training loss—while the pretrained weights remain frozen.
At − 70 % -70\% compression, LSP brings Llama-2-7B to 10.9 10.9 WikiText-2 perplexity and 42.2 % 42.2\% mean zero-shot accuracy, versus 13.3 13.3 and 36.0 % 36.0\% for the strongest baseline.

papers.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression

papers.summary: Derives a low-rank approximation to Muon and implements it using matrix multiplications. Its ReLoRA run ties the best reported final validation loss, while SFT results vary by model and evaluation.
papers.relevance: Directly tests optimization geometry and practical behavior of low-rank adapters.

evidence.quote: We derive a method for training LoRA adapters with Muon by taking a first-order approximation of the spectral-norm-regularized steepest descent objective.

While our results are both model- and eval-dependent, sMuon performs strongly overall, especially when combined with the Moonlight-16B-A3B base model, a Muon-pretrained model (Tables 1 and 2 ). sMuon also achieved the joint-best validation loss in the ReLoRA pretraining setting (Table 3 ).

papers.title: Approximate Muon with low-rank adapters

papers.summary: Normalizes LoRA down-projection matrices during training or only at initialization. The abstract reports faster convergence and improved stability across pretraining and fine-tuning settings.
papers.relevance: Targets LoRA training dynamics without adding trainable parameters or inference-time computation.

evidence.quote: We further show that the same normalization can be applied only at initialization, improving standard LoRA without requiring repeated normalization throughout training.
Across pretraining, supervised finetuning, and reinforcement learning, NoRA consistently accelerates convergence, improves performance and training stability, and mitigates catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation

papers.summary: Proposes neuron-wise normalization after Muon orthogonalization to balance update norms, with a distributed FSDP2 implementation described in the available excerpt.
papers.relevance: Matches interest in Muon and scalable LLM optimization, but its truncated abstract does not establish measured efficiency gains.

evidence.quote: NorMuon addresses this imbalance by maintaining second-order momentum statistics for each neuron and applying row-wise normalization after orthogonalization, ensuring balanced parameter utilization while preserving Muon's conditioning benefits.
To enable practical deployment at scale, we develop an efficient distributed implementation under the FSDP2 framework

papers.title: NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable

papers.summary: Studies how batch size and gradient noise affect optimizer comparisons in language-model pretraining. The abstract reports that optimizer rankings change with batch size despite hyperparameter tuning.
papers.relevance: Useful when evaluating training-efficiency claims across batch regimes and model scales.

evidence.quote: the best optimizer for language model pretraining changes with batch size even after extensive hyperparameter tuning.
gradient noise drives a bias-variance tradeoff in preconditioning that can reverse optimizer rankings across batch sizes

papers.title: The Best Optimizer Depends on Batch Size

papers.summary: Uses offline examples and hard negatives to train an embedding-based relevance filter before expensive LLM evaluation. Its reported evaluation concerns agent policies, not papers.
papers.relevance: Suggests a two-stage relevance-filter design for the research-digest harness.

evidence.quote: a lightweight first-stage relevance filter developed for Parlant 4.0 that removes at least 30% of candidate policies before downstream evaluation while preserving high recall.
An independent logistic classifier trained on their embeddings then predicts relevance using embeddings and vector dot products, with no per-turn LLM calls.

papers.title: Signals and Queries: Token-Efficient Agentic Context Discovery

papers.summary: Treats an agent’s context as a file the model can update. The abstract reports accuracy and compute improvements on several context-management tasks.
papers.relevance: Informs context-management choices for a digest agent, while differing from an application-controlled harness.

evidence.quote: We implement this by treating the context as a file and allowing the model to make unrestricted updates to this file.
11.4% higher accuracy with 21.5% fewer FLOPs on BrowseComp-Plus, 5% higher scores with 59% fewer FLOPs on 12-hour EdgeBench

papers.title: Context Language Models

papers.summary: Evaluates agents that adapt by rewriting their prompts, memory, skills, or harness from feedback. The abstract reports a stability cost from self-modification across drifting task streams.
papers.relevance: Directly bears on whether a handwritten digest harness should permit self-modification and how to evaluate it.

evidence.quote: they adapt by rewriting their own harness, such as prompts, memory, and skills, from task feedback while the model weights stay frozen.
higher plasticity consistently comes at the cost of stability.

papers.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?

papers.summary: Reviews reasoning-search loops through retrieval coupling, controller design, knowledge source, and grounding strictness.
papers.relevance: Closely matches a digest agent’s iterative paper retrieval, evidence integration, and stopping decisions.

evidence.quote: treating retrieval as an action within an iterative agentic loop rather than a one-shot preprocessing step.
interleaving planning, querying, retrieval, integration, verification, and stopping.
